title: Modals: Advice & Obligation
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Ahora sabes dar consejos y expresar obligaciones en el entorno laboral.

parts.visual: Consejo (Advice): SHOULD (Debería) / SHOULDN'T (No debería). Ej: You should save your document. You shouldn't arrive late. (Es una buena idea, pero no es obligatorio).
parts.audio: Advice. We use SHOULD and SHOULDN'T. For example: You should save your document. You shouldn't arrive late. It is a good idea, but it is not mandatory.

parts.visual: Obligación (Obligation): HAVE TO / HAS TO (Tener que). Ej: I have to wear a uniform (Es obligatorio por regla). Negativo: DON'T HAVE TO (No tienes que / No es necesario, pero puedes hacerlo si quieres). Ej: You don't have to work on Sunday.
parts.audio: Obligation. We use HAVE TO or HAS TO. For example: I have to wear a uniform. It is a rule. In the negative: DON'T HAVE TO. This means it is not necessary, but you can do it if you want. Example: You don't have to work on Sunday.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el verbo modal correcto (consejo, obligación o falta de obligación).

questions.question: You ____ save your work frequently so you don't lose it. (Consejo / Deberías).
I ____ wear a suit to the office. It's the company rule. (Tengo que / Obligación externa).
questions.explanation: Regla de la empresa = obligación externa = have to.

questions.question: You ____ be rude to the customers! (Consejo fuerte / No deberías).
Today is a holiday. You ____ work today. (No es necesario / No tienes que).
questions.explanation: Don't have to = no es necesario/no tienes la obligación.

questions.question: She ____ attend the meeting. She is the speaker! (Tiene que - Obligación).
We ____ arrive at the airport two hours before the flight. (Obligación de la aerolínea).
I think we ____ hire more people. We have too much work. (Consejo/Opinión).
questions.explanation: Con 'I think' normalmente damos una opinión o consejo: should.

questions.question: He ____ wear a tie. The dress code is casual. (No es necesario).
questions.explanation: No es necesario (he) = doesn't have to.

questions.question: ____ I call the client now or later? (Pedir consejo: ¿Debería?).
Do I ____ pay for the coffee? No, it's free. (Obligación: ¿Tengo que?).
You ____ check the numbers again. There is a mistake. (Deberías).
You ____ open that email. It looks like a virus! (No deberías).
The boss is busy. You ____ wait here. (Tienes que).
You ____ send the report today. Tomorrow is fine. (No es necesario).
questions.explanation: Tomorrow is fine -> no es obligatorio hacerlo hoy = don't have to.

questions.question: What time do we ____ leave? (Obligación: ¿A qué hora tenemos que...?).
You ____ drink so much coffee. It's bad for you. (Consejo negativo).
He ____ wake up at 5 AM every day for work. (Tiene que).
You ____ apologize. It was my fault. (No tienes que).
questions.explanation: Falta de obligación = don't have to.

questions.question: They ____ sign the contract before Friday. It's a legal requirement. (Tienen que).
I think you ____ talk to the manager about your idea. (Deberías).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe should, shouldn't, have to, has to, o don't have to.

questions.question: You ____ save your work. (Deberías - consejo)
You ____ arrive late. (No deberías - consejo negativo)
I ____ wear a uniform. (Tengo que - regla)
She ____ attend the meeting. (Tiene que - obligación de ella)
You ____ ____ ____ work on Sunday. (No es necesario/No tienes que - 3 palabras)
He ____ ____ ____ wear a tie. (No es necesario para él - 3 palabras)
____ I call the client? (¿Debería yo?)
Do I ____ ____ pay? (¿Tengo que?)
We ____ arrive early. (Tenemos que)
You ____ open that email! (No deberías - es un virus)

pairs.target: No tienes que / No es necesario
Él no tiene que / No es necesario para él
